Reserves

You: pawn 0, silver 0, gold 0, bishop 0, rook 0. House: pawn 0, silver 0, gold 0, bishop 0, rook 0.

Movement and promotion

You move upward, house downward. King: one square any direction. Gold: forward three, sideways two, backward straight. Silver: forward three and backward diagonals. Pawn: forward one. Rook: orthogonal rays. Bishop: diagonal rays. Entering OR leaving the far rank offers promotion: silver/pawn become gold; rook adds diagonal king steps; bishop adds orthogonal king steps. Pawn promotion is mandatory. Captures return the unpromoted type to your reserve.

Legal drops and endings

Drop instead of moving, into an empty square. A pawn cannot drop on the far rank, a file containing your own unpromoted pawn, or deliver immediate checkmate. Every move must escape self-check. Checkmate wins; stalemate, fourfold repetition, or 200 plies draws. The house searches your possible replies, including reserve drops.

How to play
5×5 board with king, rook, bishop, gold, silver and one single-step pawn per side (six units each). In the default deal, human back row A5–E5 is King, Gold, Silver, Bishop, Rook with pawn A4; house back row A1–E1 is Rook, Bishop, Silver, Gold, King with pawn E2. That default opening has twelve occupied squares and thirteen free; Another deal may start with an advanced silver or a pawn in reserve. Piece moves fixed and illustrated. Capture demotes and transfers unit into captor reserve; drop replaces a move. Promotion available when entering or leaving the far row, with promoted movement printed. Pawn drops cannot share a file with own unpromoted pawn or give immediate mate; no self-check. Four repeated positions draw.
Checkmate wins/losses; no legal move while not checked draws in this explicitly simplified ruleset. Public 100-turn draw bound.
